To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the meaning of an utterance can be determined only by the interaction between the basic components of this sentence, 2) the meaning of each basic component is determined by the contribution of the different other components, and 3) this meaning is determined simultaneously with the other components of the utterance.
meaning construction is based on a gestalt process and is the result of an interaction between all the components of the utterance.

the comprehension process is based on the interaction of the basic components of a linguistic expression (words, syntactic markers, positional relations, and constructions) and that the meaning of a sentence is the result of a dynamic process of construction of meaning that is gestalt-like in the sense that the contribution of each component is determined by the contribution of the others.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of meaning construction in the comprehension of utterances, and more precisely, with the question of the contribution of the different basic components (lexical units, grammatical units, and positional relations between units) in this process of construction.

the study of meaning construction from a dynamic perspective, in which the different components of an utterance interact with each other and contribute simultaneously to the construction of a global meaning.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
language is not a code but rather a process, a dynamic and complex process of meaning construction.
language is a dynamic process of construction of meaning, and that meaning is not a static object that can be extracted from a linguistic structure.
the meaning of an utterance results from the interaction between all the linguistic units present in the utterances and the interaction between these units and the context of the utterance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
meaning is not a static product of a compositional process but rather the dynamic product of the interaction of different components of the linguistic units.
meaning is the result of a dynamic and interactive process between different components.
the comprehension process is based on an interaction between the basic components of the utterance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meaning construction is not a simple matter of syntax, but rather a dynamic process that is sensitive to all the different components of a linguistic utterance.
a gestalt compositionality model can account for the construction of meaning in language comprehension.

the process of meaning construction is not a simple linear process of syntactic analysis followed by semantic analysis, but rather the result of the interaction of several components of the utterance.
